title: Gepotidacin versus nitrofurantoin in uncomplicated urinary tract infection
topic_state: POOLED WITH SUBSTANTIAL HETEROGENEITY -- k=2, I2=70.5%, no conclusion drawn
verification_basis: Both registrations read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18: conditions, arm groups with types, registered primary outcome measures, and the POSTED RESULTS counts and denominators used in the pool.
provenance: REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Every count and denominator in this pool is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used and no value is imported.

primary.outcome: therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure visit

pooled.measure_note: Copied from the analysis block, where it already stood. The generator reads pooled["measure"]; our schema carried it one level up. NOT a new claim -- the same value, placed where the consumer looks.

pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends the Hartung-Knapp adjustment where k is small. At k=2 it uses t on ONE degree of freedom, whose critical value is 12.71 against the normal 1.96, so the interval is very much wider. IT IS SHOWN ALONGSIDE RATHER THAN INSTEAD, because presenting only the narrow interval would overstate what two trials establish and presenting only the wide one would understate two large concordant trials. A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never NARROW the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_k2: I-squared and tau-squared at k=2 are WEAK evidence about consistency in either direction. Two points cannot demonstrate agreement, and a low value here means only that the two estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect -- not that one is established.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: Higgins I-squared = (Q - df) / Q, clamped at 0. Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.2.
heterogeneity.i2_definition_evidence: Decided by recomputing BOTH definitions from this object's own per-trial inputs: Higgins gives 70.4623 and REML/metafor gives 70.4623 against the stored 70.5000.
heterogeneity.i2_key_aliases_note: i2 and i2_pct mirror i2_percent, which this object already carried. THE GENERATOR READS het["i2"] / het["i2_pct"]; our schema wrote i2_percent, so the page rendered "I-squared not stated" -- which was the GENERATOR BEHAVING CORRECTLY, marking an absence rather than inventing a zero. SAME VALUE, PLACED WHERE THE CONSUMER LOOKS. The definition is declared in i2_definition: this is Higgins (Q-df)/Q.

per_trial.label: EAGLE-2
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. The COUNTS are read from the registry's posted results; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown so both can be checked.

per_trial.label: EAGLE-3
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. The COUNTS are read from the registry's posted results; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown so both can be checked.

primary.denominator_handling: Both trials post responder and failure counts that sum exactly to the posted denominator (162+158=320, 135+152=287, 162+115=277, 115+149=264). Nothing is unaccounted.
primary.why_this_topic_pools_when_most_do_not: Of 62 infectious-disease topics, this is one of the few that survives all four limbs without reconciliation: the SAME experimental drug in the experimental arm of both trials, the SAME active comparator, the SAME registered primary outcome measured the same way, and the SAME infection. The eleven topics closed on 2026-08-18 failed because one of those four differed. This is what a poolable topic looks like.

published_synthesis_comparison.status: NOT DONE -- recorded as owed rather than claimed
published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: A published meta-analysis or regulatory review pooling these two trials on this outcome has NOT been searched for or read. Until it is, this object states an estimate that has not been checked against anyone else's. That is a gap in this page, and it is named here rather than left for a reader to discover.
published_synthesis_comparison.why_it_matters_here: Both trial pairs are registration trials for a new antibiotic, so a regulatory review almost certainly pools them and would be the strongest available comparator.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED, and a pooled estimate without one is an arithmetic result, not a graded finding. NOT non-inferiority or superiority: both trials were designed as non-inferiority studies against an active comparator, and a risk ratio near 1 with an interval spanning 1 is the EXPECTED result of a successful non-inferiority trial rather than evidence of no difference. NOT that the pooled interval is reliable at k=2 -- see the Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest width. NOT agreement with any published synthesis; none has been checked.

handbook_authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
handbook_authority.estimator_note: REML is the Handbook 6.5 default tau-squared estimator. At k=2 the Handbook notes that random-effects estimates of between-study variance are very imprecise, and 10.10.4.5 recommends the Hartung-Knapp adjustment where k is small.

primary.HETEROGENEITY_WARNING_READ_BEFORE_THE_PO: THE TWO TRIALS DISAGREE AND THE POOLED POINT SHOULD NOT BE READ AS THE ANSWER. I-squared is 70.5% and tau-squared 0.0172 on TWO trials. EAGLE-2 gives RR 1.08 with an interval spanning 1 (0.91-1.27); EAGLE-3 gives RR 1.34 with an interval EXCLUDING 1 (1.13-1.59). One trial finds gepotidacin no better than nitrofurantoin and the other finds it better. The random-effects interval (0.97-1.49) spans 1, and the Hartung-Knapp interval at one degree of freedom (0.29-4.89) is uninformative. THIS TOPIC HAS A POOLED NUMBER AND NOT A CONCLUSION.
primary.why_this_warning_is_here_and_not_a_footn: A published olmesartan review in our own error taxonomy reports I-squared = 100%, pools final values, and interprets the estimate anyway. That pattern -- disclosure treated as discharging the obligation the disclosure creates -- is CLASS 2 in TAXONOMY-PUBLISHED-SYNTHESIS-ERRORS.md, and the taxonomy was written the same day this pool was built. It caught this build. The consequence is placed in the same block as the number rather than in a note below it, because that is the difference between reporting heterogeneity and acting on it.

heterogeneity_cause_CHECKED_AND_NOT_EXPL.what_was_checked: Registered ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA and the primary outcome DEFINITION for both trials, read from ClinicalTrials.gov on 2026-08-18. The asymmetry pointed at the trials rather than the drug -- the comparator arm behaved consistently (47.0% then 43.6%) while the experimental arm moved (50.6% then 58.5%) -- so population and adjudication were the cheapest candidate causes.
heterogeneity_cause_CHECKED_AND_NOT_EXPL.eligibility: NEAR-IDENTICAL. Both enrol FEMALE participants only, aged >=12 years, weight >=40 kg, with 2 or more signs or symptoms of acute cystitis with onset <96 hours, and nitrite or pyuria (>15 WBC/HPF or 3+/large leukocyte esterase) on a pretreatment clean-catch midstream sample. Both exclude nursing-home residence, BMI >=40 (or >=35 with obesity-related conditions), study-drug sensitivity, and immunocompromise. The criteria are the same programme written twice.
heterogeneity_cause_CHECKED_AND_NOT_EXPL.outcome_definition: THE SAME COMPOSITE in both: therapeutic success requires BOTH microbiological success (qualifying uropathogens reduced to <10^3 CFU/mL without other systemic antimicrobials before test-of-cure) AND clinical success (resolution of cystitis symptoms), with lack of either -- INCLUDING MISSING ASSESSMENTS -- counted as failure. Both analyse the SAME population: micro-ITT susceptible to nitrofurantoin, Interim Analysis Set. Wording differs trivially (EAGLE-2 says signs and symptoms where EAGLE-3 says symptoms; EAGLE-3 adds a parenthesis about antibiotics on the day of the test-of-cure visit). Nothing there redefines success.
heterogeneity_cause_CHECKED_AND_NOT_EXPL.VERDICT: THE CHEAPEST EXPLANATION IS RULED OUT AND THE HETEROGENEITY REMAINS UNEXPLAINED. Registered population and registered outcome definition do not differ in any way that would produce a 70.5% I-squared. What is NOT ruled out and cannot be from the registrations: the pathogen and RESISTANCE PROFILE at the enrolling sites, the geographic mix, and how consistently the composite was applied in practice as opposed to how it was defined. Those need the clinical study reports or a regulatory review, which have not been read. THE POOLED POINT STILL SHOULD NOT BE READ AS THE ANSWER.
heterogeneity_cause_CHECKED_AND_NOT_EXPL.cost_of_this_check: Under a minute, on data already retrieved. It did not resolve the question; it removed the answer that would have been assumed.

primary.schema_alias_note: estimator_used mirrors the estimator this pool actually used (REML, already recorded). The generator reads res["estimator_used"]; our schema wrote it as "estimator". SAME VALUE, PLACED WHERE THE CONSUMER LOOKS -- not a new claim.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_the_analysis_population_was_checked_an: CHECKED AND CLEAN. Read from the registrations on 2026-08-21: NCT04020341 registers 'Number of Participants With Therapeutic Response (Combined Per Participant Clinical and Microbiological Respon' (population: TR); NCT04187144 registers 'Number of Participants With Therapeutic Response (Combined Per Participant Clinical and Microbiological Respon' (population: TR). Both trials register the same primary in the same population, so this pool does NOT cross an analysis-population boundary. Recorded because a check that only speaks when it finds something cannot be told from a check that was never run.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_what_remains_unresolved: Whether these are non-inferiority designs is NOT established: the registration fields fetched do not use the word, and a pooled ratio from non-inferiority trials answers a different question from a superiority pool. Unresolved, not assumed.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_the_published_pool_of_the_same_two_tri: THE SPONSOR'S OWN POOLED ANALYSIS OF THESE EXACT TWO TRIALS SPLITS BY NITROFURANTOIN SUSCEPTIBILITY, AND THE EFFECT IS MORE THAN TWICE AS LARGE IN THE NOT-SUSCEPTIBLE STRATUM: therapeutic success difference +9.6% [4.1, 15.2] where the uropathogen is susceptible against +20.8% [9.2, 32.4] where it is not (PMID 42413960, Clin Infect Dis 2026, EAGLE-2 NCT04020341 and EAGLE-3 NCT04187144). THIS POOL COLLAPSES THAT SPLIT, so its single ratio is an average over two populations the published analysis keeps apart.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_and_the_scales_differ_so_no_discrepanc: They report a RISK DIFFERENCE in percentage points and this object pools a RISK RATIO; theirs is micro-ITT and this object's registered outcome text names no analysis population. Their interval excludes zero and this one includes one, and those are not contradictory statements about one quantity.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.c_whose_analysis_it_is: The pooled analysis is by the sponsor's investigators. That does not make it wrong and it is the most direct evidence about these two trials, but it is stated rather than treated as an independent referee.

r_output._what_this_is: The console output of the fit, captured as it was printed. NOT re-typed and NOT summarised -- P46 limb 4 asks for the model output, and a paraphrase of model output is a claim about a model rather than the model's own words.
r_output.call: rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, method = "REML")  and the same fit with test = "knha"
r_output.inputs_derivation: yi = log(point); sei = (log(ci_high) - log(ci_low)) / (2 * 1.959964). Read from this object's own per_trial rows. NO COUNT IS INVENTED and no interval is re-typed.
r_output.hartung_knapp_note: Shown BESIDE the unadjusted interval, never instead of it. At k = 2 the t critical value is 12.7062 on 1 degree of freedom, which is why the adjusted interval is very wide -- that width is the honest one at this k.
r_output.what_k_equals_2_means: Two trials cannot inform a between-study variance. tau^2 is estimated with ONE degree of freedom and Q on 1 df carries almost no information about heterogeneity. THAT IS A PROPERTY OF THE EVIDENCE -- there are two trials -- and not of our access to it.
r_output.interval_method: REML with the unadjusted Wald interval, and the same fit under Hartung-Knapp beside it. THE HOUSE INTERVAL FLOORS THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR AT max(1, SE_knha/SE_unadjusted); metafor's raw unfloored value is printed separately and flagged where it is narrower than the unadjusted interval.
r_output.why_this_was_re_run: THE PREVIOUS STORED OUTPUT LABELLED metafor's RAW knha INTERVAL 'Hartung-Knapp' with no qualifier. render_contract: THE BLOCK LIST IS DECLARED HERE, NOT IN THE PROJECTOR. scripts/project_topic_page.py maps a block TYPE to a formatter and knows nothing about which blocks this topic has. Adding a sixth block is an edit to THIS list. A missing path is a REFUSAL, never a placeholder.
question: In adults with uncomplicated urinary tract infection, does gepotidacin differ from nitrofurantoin in therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological success) at the test-of-cure visit?

outcomes.name: Therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure
outcomes.definition: Therapeutic success requires BOTH microbiological success (qualifying uropathogens reduced to <10^3 CFU/mL without other systemic antimicrobials before test-of-cure) AND clinical success (resolution of cystitis symptoms). Lack of either, INCLUDING MISSING ASSESSMENTS, is failure. Read from both registrations 2026-08-18; the two definitions are identical.
outcomes.definition_note: Both registrations define therapeutic success identically and were read on 2026-08-18. Eligibility is also near-identical across the two trials, so neither the population nor the endpoint definition explains the substantial heterogeneity this topic carries.

schema_fields_added_2026_08_18: question, outcomes, carried_contrasts and sources were absent and the generator requires all four. THEY WERE FILLED WITH CONTENT ESTABLISHED TOPIC BY TOPIC, NOT WITH EMPTY VALUES TO MAKE A BUILD SUCCEED. carried_contrasts is [] and sources is {} because both are GENUINELY EMPTY for this topic -- it is a k=2 pairwise pool with no carried network contrasts, and the same two fields are empty on acs-antiplatelet-review, which builds. An empty value written merely to pass a schema check would be the defaulted-field lie at the schema layer, and it would be published.

risk_of_bias.tool: RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials)

NCT04020341.registered_masking: DOUBLE -- participant and investigator; THE OUTCOMES ASSESSOR IS NOT AMONG THE MASKED ROLES
NCT04020341.result_assessed: therapeutic response, combined per-participant CLINICAL AND MICROBIOLOGICAL response -- ONE OF TWO REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOMES

D1_randomisation_process.reason: allocation is recorded as RANDOMIZED on the design module.
D1_randomisation_process.what_is_NOT_established: The concealment MECHANISM is not on the registry and no publication was read. LOW is scored on the recorded allocation, not on a mechanism nobody here has seen.

resolved_2026_08_21.the_text_that_decides_it: RoB 2 guidance 2019, Box 4, signalling question 1.1: "Answer 'No information' if the only information about randomization methods is a statement that the study is randomized." And section 4.4: "A judgement of low risk of bias requires that the trial has an adequate method of concealing the allocation sequence from those involved in enrolling participants, and there are no concerns about generation of the allocation sequence." Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 8.3 names the domain's three components.
resolved_2026_08_21.why_this_is_not_an_adjudicated_dispute: A blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. THAT WOULD ORDINARILY BE A DISPUTE TO ADJUDICATE. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.

It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred to; the guidance is being applied.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_the_registry_gives_and_does_not: A ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: RANDOMIZED`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
resolved_2026_08_21.how_this_maps_to_the_tool_s_algorithm: The tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a DOMAIN judgement of SOME CONCERNS. This project writes NO_INFORMATION on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the OVERALL at SOME_CONCERNS. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_does_not_change: NO OVERALL RATING AND NO GRADE CERTAINTY MOVES. All 51 judgements were already capped at SOME_CONCERNS or HIGH by another NO_INFORMATION domain.
resolved_2026_08_21.what_would_close_it_properly: The trial publications or protocols, which carry sequence generation and concealment. Neither was read. Until one is, LOW is not available on this domain for any result in this corpus.

grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.
grade.not_rated_up: No domain is rated UP. Rating up for a large effect, a dose-response gradient or opposing plausible confounding applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials, which start HIGH and can only be rated down.

steps.reason: BOTH results are SOME_CONCERNS and the driver is named: the OUTCOMES ASSESSOR IS NOT MASKED (masking is DOUBLE -- participant and investigator) on an endpoint whose clinical half is a judgement, and each trial registers TWO primaries of which this review pools one without recording the choice. D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION.

The two trials disagree in direction of conclusion: 1.0762 (0.9138 to 1.2676) INCLUDES no difference and 1.3426 (1.1334 to 1.5904) EXCLUDES it. The stored refit gives I-squared 70.48%, Q 3.3879 on 1 df, p = 0.0657. At k = 2 that I-squared is not itself evidence, but the non-overlap of conclusions is.

steps.move: LOW to VERY LOW, down 1 level(s)
steps.reason: The pooled result is ONE OF TWO REGISTERED PRIMARY OUTCOMES, chosen without a recorded reason, and the endpoint COMBINES a microbiological result with a clinical judgement. The quantity pooled is therefore not cleanly the quantity a reader would take 'therapeutic response' to mean.

steps.move: VERY LOW -- already at the floor, no further downgrade applied
steps.reason: k = 2. The Hartung-Knapp interval is RR 1.2007 (0.2946 to 4.8937) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, and the unadjusted interval crosses no difference. The rating cannot fall below VERY LOW, so this domain is recorded as warranting a downgrade that the scale cannot express.
k = 2. A funnel plot and its asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is NOT ASSESSABLE rather than 'undetected'.

primary.summary: VERY LOW certainty. Both contributing results carry unmasked outcome assessment on a partly-judgemental endpoint; the two trials disagree on whether the effect excludes no difference; the pooled quantity is one of two registered primaries; and k = 2 cannot support precision.

published_comparison.THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_COMPARISON_2026_08_2: THE SPONSOR'S OWN POOLED ANALYSIS OF THESE EXACT TWO TRIALS SPLITS BY NITROFURANTOIN SUSCEPTIBILITY, AND THE EFFECT IS MORE THAN TWICE AS LARGE IN THE NOT-SUSCEPTIBLE STRATUM: therapeutic success difference +9.6% [4.1, 15.2] where the uropathogen is susceptible against +20.8% [9.2, 32.4] where it is not (PMID 42413960, Clin Infect Dis 2026, EAGLE-2 NCT04020341 and EAGLE-3 NCT04187144). THIS POOL COLLAPSES THAT SPLIT, so its single ratio is an average over two populations the published analysis keeps apart. They report a RISK DIFFERENCE in percentage points and this object pools a RISK RATIO; theirs is micro-ITT and this object's registered outcome text names no analysis population. Their interval excludes zero and this one includes one, and those are not contradictory statements about one quantity. The pooled analysis is by the sponsor's investigators. That does not make it wrong and it is the most direct evidence about these two trials, but it is stated rather than treated as an independent referee.

manuscript.introduction:
This review asks: In adults with uncomplicated urinary tract infection, does gepotidacin differ from nitrofurantoin in therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological success) at the test-of-cure visit?

It pools 2 randomised trials, against nitrofurantoin.

The outcome pooled is Therapeutic response (combined clinical and microbiological), test-of-cure.

Every count and denominator behind those estimates is read as follows. REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Every count and denominator in this pool is read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results. No publication figure is used and no value is imported.

WHAT THIS PARAGRAPH DOES NOT CONTAIN, AND WHY. Why the question is open, what this review adds to what was already known, and what the pooled effect means clinically are JUDGEMENTS, not fields, and no field on this object can back them. They are owed and they are not written here; assembling them from the numbers above would be inventing a rationale to fit a result. Everything above is derived from stored fields and nothing in it is authored.
